Which Function Should I Use?

Source: vignettes/choose-model.Rmd
choose-model.Rmd

Start from two questions: what kind of outcome do you have, and how were the observations collected? The tables below point to the function, the approach where one is needed, and the effect measure that appears in the table. Every function shares the same arguments for exposures, adjustment variables, formatting and export.

Binary outcomes

An outcome with two values, such as disease or no disease.

Question Function approach Reported as
Odds of the outcome uni_reg(), multi_reg() "logit" Odds ratio
Odds with sparse data or separation uni_reg(), multi_reg() "firth" Odds ratio (Firth)
Risk of the outcome, relative uni_reg(), multi_reg() "logbinomial" or "robpoisson" Risk ratio
Risk of the outcome, absolute (two groups) risk_difference() none Risk difference, NNTB/NNTH
Matched case-control sets conditional_logit_reg() none Matched odds ratio
Clustered observations (clinics, schools) multilevel_reg() "logit" Odds ratio, random intercept

"robpoisson" (Poisson with robust standard errors) is a dependable alternative when a log-binomial model fails to converge.

Counts and rates

Question Function approach Reported as
Event counts uni_reg(), multi_reg() "poisson" Incidence rate ratio
Over-dispersed counts uni_reg(), multi_reg() "negbin" Incidence rate ratio

Continuous outcomes

Question Function approach Reported as
Mean of the outcome uni_reg(), multi_reg() "linear" Beta (difference in means)
Clustered observations multilevel_reg() "linear" Beta, random intercept

Outcomes with three or more categories

Question Function Reported as
Ordered categories (mild, moderate, severe) ordinal_reg() Common odds ratio (proportional odds)
Unordered categories multinomial_reg() Odds ratio for each category versus the reference category

Time to event

Question Function Reported as
Describe survival over time km_plot(), survival_summary(), survival_prob() Kaplan-Meier estimates
Compare survival curves logrank_test(), rmst_table() Log-rank p-value, restricted mean survival time
Hazard of the event cox_reg() Hazard ratio
Survival time itself surv_reg() Time ratio (accelerated failure time)
One event type in the presence of others cuminc_plot(), competing_risk_reg() Cumulative incidence, subdistribution hazard ratio

Check the proportional-hazards assumption of a Cox model with check_ph().

Repeating an analysis within groups

stratified_uni_reg() and stratified_multi_reg() fit the same model within each level of a stratifier, for example by sex or study site.

Beyond a single estimate

Question Function
Is a variable a confounder or effect modifier? identify_confounder(), interaction_models()
How much of an effect acts through a mediator? mediation_analysis()
Does the model fit and converge? check_convergence(), check_collinearity(), plot_model_fit()
Which of several prespecified models fits best? compare_models(), select_models()
